en: In the language of India: *Acintyakramopadeśa-nāma*.
In the language of Tibet: *bsam gyis mi khyab pa’i rim pa’i man ngag* (The Instruction on the Stages of the Inconceivable). Homage to the glorious Vajrasattva! Homage to the Blessed One, Lokeśvara!
Homage to Vajrasattva!

Having prostrated before the inconceivable, non-dual, and all-pervading one, who is born from the womb of the supreme wisdom, I shall correctly write down that which has been transmitted through the lineage of the venerable Bhadrapāda. (1)
The great secret of wisdom and means, characterized by inconceivable compassion,
arises spontaneously as gnosis, whose sphere transcends the path of speech.

And this Self-Existent One is not perceived as having the nature of an entity—the supreme non-duality—nor by way of non-existence; so too are the Bodhisattvas together with the Holder of the Vajra. (3)
Distinction by way of the dichotomy of eternalism and nihilism is not the ultimate truth; it is called non-duality.
This cultivation, however, is not an intrinsic nature; it is neither apprehension nor emptiness.
When both are investigated, non-dual knowledge blazes forth;
for everything has a non-dual form, and this duality does not exist.
The supreme, inconceivable gnosis has the form of equalized flavor;
through the yoga of conceptual gnosis, one should not cultivate that which is non-dual and supreme. (6)
The non-conceptual and inconceivable state of the Holder of the Bliss-Vajra is not attained;
for origination is the cause of conceptualization, and non-origination is likewise [the cause]. (7)
Devoid of both forms and free from the relationship of the perfumed and the perfume,
gnosis devoid of latent impressions has come down through the lineage of the venerable Bhadrapāda. (8)
The Self-Existent (Svayambhū) is indeed waveless, devoid of all conceptual constructions,
the very nature of both existence and non-existence, and free from the bondage of the two-fold latent impressions.
By its non-conceptual nature, it is inconceivable and cannot be divided;
yet the jewel of the mind is defiled by the web of the stains of conceptual construction. (10)
Because of the removal of impurities, the Buddha is called non-dual gnosis;
all things, which are non-conceptual in nature, should always be perceived by yogins in this way. (11)
This cultivation of meditative concentration has been taught by Bhadrapāda;
its intrinsic nature neither arises nor perishes.
That non-dual knowledge is called free from all conceptual constructions;
it is designated as "imagination" by the Buddhas, Vajradhara, and others. (13)
It generates the non-conceptual object of the glorious Mahāsukha-vajrin;
all worlds are supported by external and internal conceptualization. (14)
Non-dual knowledge, free from both duality and non-duality, arises of itself:
there is no cultivation in non-existence, nor is there cultivation in existence. (15)
The state of blissful consciousness is unattainable, inconceivable, and non-dual;
it is that which is to be contemplated within all sentient beings, established in the womb of wisdom. 16.
With the arrow of the awakening of compassion, one should pierce the target, which is great bliss—
completely free from all doubt, beyond duality, and supremely auspicious.
Equal to space and free from conceptual construction, that is called non-duality;
through the application of the inconceivable state, one should discern all phenomena. 18.
It was taught by Bhadrapāda as having come down through the lineage of Dharmapāda:
that the world is fashioned in the form of the universe through the nature of a single fusion. 19.
By the Lord of Great Bliss, through the distinction of the non-dual form, those who advocate for the perception of emptiness or for false doctrines have been led astray. (20)
Bound by the fetters of conceptual thought, they do not perceive glorious bliss;
nor is there any other "evil conceptualization" apart from the purity of wisdom and means. (21)
The non-dual gnosis of Mahāyoga is indeed the single Great Bliss;
all beings, both moving and stationary, are established in non-duality. (22)
Pure by their very nature from the beginning, they are utterly stainless in the peaceful expanse of space;
because they are non-dual, this is a mere name, yet even that name does not exist. (23)
The non-dual great bliss is devoid of the characteristics of both the Vedas and the knower of the Vedas;
it is neither the Buddha nor the object of the intellect, for it is inconceivable by its very nature. || 24 ||
Indeed, everything has that as its intrinsic nature; it is self-existent and beyond thought.
All living beings on earth are destroyed by the web of conceptual constructions.
Non-dual gnosis is indeed one, entirely free from all conceptual constructions;
as long as the two heaps—eternalism and nihilism—do not exist, [it remains so]. 26.
The non-apprehension of the middle, however, is non-dual knowledge, marvelous, free from all conceptual proliferation, and stainless like space. (27)
That which is severed from the web of conceptual construction is the inconceivable, non-dual, supreme [reality].
Those who are pierced by the essence of non-duality become like wood, stone, or clay.
They attain the form of the deity as taught by Bhadrapāda;
they become one with the single form of the equal flavor of wisdom, skillful means, and great compassion. (29)
In that [state], non-dual gnosis, which is great bliss, is accomplished;
it transcends form, sound, and taste, and is devoid of smell, touch, and the rest. || 30 ||
The supreme, non-dual gnosis consists of the dharmadhātu; it is pure, liberated from all conceptual construction, and devoid of the grasped and the grasper. || 31 ||
The abode is pure by its very nature, non-dual, ultimate, indestructible, unarisen, syllable-less, and without foundation. || 32 ||
This Mahāmudrā is the supreme non-dual knowledge, absolutely beyond extremes;
it is said that the mind is the support for both defects and virtues. (33)
In that state, a knowledge centered on pervasion arises spontaneously by its very nature, free from all waves;
this knowledge arises of itself, and one should not conceptualize anything at all.
For this dharma of the Buddhas is inconceivable, the non-dual state, perfectly stainless, utterly pure, and devoid of both the object of meditation and the meditator. (35)
Indeed, through non-conceptualization, everything is seen as the arising of glorious bliss—the forms of many deities, such as the embodiment of Vajrasattva and others. (36)
The entire form of the Buddha, the maṇḍala of the host of yoginīs, all the wrathful kings, and likewise the vidyā-devis; || 37 ||
The divine maṇḍala-circle, however, is stainless and has the appearance of light;
it consists of the Sūtras together with the Vinaya, as well as the system of the Pāramitās. (38)
Likewise, the mantras and mudrās, the vidyās, and the incitement within the heart;
indeed, the entire discourse on mantras, the maṇḍala, and the rite of fire-offerings (homa). || 39 ||
The procedure for recitation and worship arises spontaneously in due order:
the Śaiva, Saura, Ārhata, and likewise the Vaiṣṇava [systems]. (40)
This yoga of the state of omniscience is inconceivable and free from conceptual construction. || 41 ||
The divine [tantra] called Samantabhadra, which is non-dual like a wish-fulfilling gem,
contains the collection of the netherworld sword, the pill, the yakṣiṇī, and the foot-stamp.
Rasāñjana and the divine [substances] are accomplished spontaneously; it is not otherwise.
Through non-conceptual resolve, everything arises of its own accord. (43)
The mantra-practitioner should not cultivate existence, nor should he cultivate non-existence.
What can be said of him? He is neither a Buddha, nor Śiva, nor Viṣṇu, nor an Arhat.
For him there exists no name, no form, and no characteristic of color;
he possesses a divine aggregate of aggregates that assumes the guise of an illusionist and is pure by nature. 45.
Its form is naturally luminous, arising as eternal bliss and happiness;
it is devoid of body, speech, and mind, a mirror-like mass of light-networks.
The form of the bliss of supreme joy, the eternally arisen great bliss, is expressed through the articulation of names and syllables by means of the application of the words of instruction. (47)

Otherwise, that which transcends the path of speech could never be expressed; yet, through your effortless play, you have revealed the desired meaning by means of the form of the *naya* systems at the conclusion of your activity. (48)
The time for the secret worship was taught by Bhadrapāda through non-dual knowledge, by virtue of its nature being of a single form. (49)
When latent impressions (vāsanā) reach their exhaustion, Buddhahood is certainly attained;
this occurs through the various distinctions of colors and by means of the application of diverse philosophical systems. || 50 ||

One whose mind is sprinkled with the impurity of latent tendencies does not perceive non-duality—that which is devoid of beginning, middle, and end, and free from both the perfected and the produced. (51)
The mind that has been relinquished is consciousness; that is the supreme non-dual gnosis.
This so-called "non-dual" was taught by the Buddha Bhadrapāda. (52)
Through the realization of that [reality], he becomes a Buddha, the supreme practitioner;
by means of the application of the words of teaching, the Buddha is conceived as non-dual. (53)
When the true nature of primordial wisdom has arisen, far removed from the stains of conceptual construction, there is neither a Buddha in the form of ultimate diversity, nor is there non-duality.
Through the grace of Bhadrapāda, by means of the yoga of hearing and repeated practice, one attains direct realization of reality and the state of non-conceptuality regarding all phenomena. (55)
I take refuge in that which is called non-duality; it should be forgiven by the yogis.
The wise should strive with effort to bring about the exhaustion of latent impressions (vāsanā). || 56 ||
Otherwise, Buddhahood would not be attained even in tens of millions of incalculable eons;
rather, through non-dual gnosis, the destruction of latent predispositions is brought about.
For one who has arisen from the exhaustion of latent impressions (vāsanā) is called a non-dual Buddha;
in the state of the Person (puruṣa) devoid of latent impressions, there are the lowest and the middling. 58.
But "Buddhahood" is said to belong to him; even a partisan position does not exist here.
In its own nature, it is devoid of intrinsic being, yet it abides as the aspect of wisdom. 59.
Through the union of those two as a single object of focus by way of the yoga of the single flavor, this supreme non-duality has been taught by Bhadrapāda. (60)
The cultivation of discourse, which consists of supreme bliss, is not to be conceptualized;
O auspicious one, this auspicious [discourse] has been taught as the cause for attaining Buddhahood. 61.
No analogy can ever be given for all phenomena;
the cognition of the eye and so forth, as well as the mind, is devoid of any state that could serve as an illustration.
This one alone is beginningless and established in infinite forms;
it is known by the supreme [means] through the grace of the Guru’s feet. 63.
Yoga is declared to be the person (puruṣa), while the practice (anuyoga) is the conventional reality (saṃvṛti).
Through the non-dual knowledge of Mahāyoga, yogins attain Buddhahood. || 64 ||
During lunar and solar eclipses, through the application of the wisdom-vajra, when non-dual gnosis has dissolved, buddhahood is attained in this very life. (65)
This union with the bliss of the welfare of others is devoid of subject and object;
it is the perfected form, free from doubt, the supreme non-dual compassion. (66)
Whatever form and the intermediate phenomenon are seen with the two eyes,
they should be viewed as the supreme non-duality in the form of ultimate bliss. (67)
That which is heard by the ears and that which is [discerned] through the differentiation of sounds—the supreme knowledge beyond sound is the non-dual, most excellent hearing (śravaṇa). || 68 ||
The tongue tastes that which is both tasteless and the most excellent of tastes;
the six tastes should be understood as a single state, the supreme non-duality. (69)
The nose and the consciousness of odor, as well as the memory of the impurities of musk and the like, are known through their nature of single fusion as the supreme non-dual. (70)
Through the nature of body and touch, by means of the distinction between birth and non-birth, and through the union of wisdom and skillful means, the supreme non-duality is perfected. (71)
It is infinite, all-pervading, and everything by virtue of the power of the light of gnosis;
it is the supreme bliss of absolute freedom, non-dual, the true happiness of a Buddha. (72)
Formative predispositions, sensation, perception, form, and consciousness itself—the body consisting of these five knowledges is the non-dual supreme of the five Buddhas. || 73 ||
Śāśvata, Akṣobhya, Ratna, Āyuḥ, and likewise Amogha—this is the single mass consisting of five; let the sixth be Mahāsukha. (74)
Earth, water, fire, air, and space— indeed,
the great arising of these five elements is non-dual awakening.

Through the mirror-like [wisdom], the wisdom of equality, the wisdom of accomplishing activities, and the wisdom of discerning the realm of phenomena, conceptual constructions—which are of the nature of imagination—are themselves the self-arisen, one, and non-dual. (76)
[Ed. p.
203] Due to the differentiation of seeing and so forth, and by virtue of the dispositions of sentient beings, there are Śaivas, Vaiṣṇavas, and Brahmans; yet the Omniscient One is one and non-dual.
The deficiency of the eye and so forth is beyond the domain of the mind;
that which is called ultimate reality is non-dual, whereas verbal proliferation is the conventional. || 78 ||
Due to the distinction of the state of ultimate reality, there is neither a Buddha nor even non-duality;
it is through the application of the space of conceptualization that verbal proliferation is spoken of.
The non-dual Buddha cannot be described otherwise than through the sequential arrangement of all the scriptures and by means of the analytical exposition of their explanations. (80)
The sixteen are declared as the cooked [offerings], while the ten are conceived as wisdom;
the Buddhas are reckoned as five, and non-duality is the sixfold veil. || 81 ||
Just as everything is seen in the reflections of the world within a mirror, so too is the inconceivable awakening of the Buddha present within this non-dual gnosis. 82.
In all the elements, by means of the causes of arising and abiding, all that is non-dual gnosis; all sentient beings have emerged from it. (83)
The oceans, mountains, trees, and whatever grasses, shrubs, and creepers there are—all have issued forth from non-dual knowledge; herein no delusion exists. (84)
Mother and father—these two do not exist together as one;
when the reality of non-dual knowledge is present, the supreme arises as everything. 85.
By means of this application of skillful methods, through the nature of the two kinds of wisdom, the state of Buddhahood is attained instantly by the yogin even in this very life. (86)
Through the yoga of inconceivable cultivation, Buddhahood is certainly attained;
[this was realized by] Paramāśva, Vīṇāpāda, Indrabhūti, and Lakṣmī. 88.
Vilāsavajra, Guṇḍerī, and the most compassionate Padmācārya—these [masters] have come down through the lineage of Dharmapāda and the succession of Bhadrapāda. (89)
The intention of all is one: the supreme non-dual gnosis;
likewise, there is the entirety of the mantra system as well as the way of the perfections (pāramitānaya).
In this [system], the non-dual Great Bliss is derived from the Sūtrānta-piṭaka and other sources;
it is the very Soma-siddhānta of the Arhats, the Sauras, the Śaivas, and others. (91)
The Vaiṣṇava dharma of Manu was taught by means of non-duality;
since there is no speech that expresses non-duality, there are no gods, asuras, or base humans.
Yet all non-dual gnosis appears as a reflection;
it is non-dual, infused with compassion, and endowed with wisdom and skillful means. || 93 ||
But the Guru, who is composed of all Buddhas and distinguished by the non-duality of emptiness—this indeed is the supreme ocean of gnosis, the doctrine of Bhadrapāda. (94)
Everything supreme arises from the form of the churning of the Ocean of Milk—namely, those who are celebrated as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Buddha, and the rest. (95)
The moon, the sun, and the stars, born from the ocean of knowledge;
Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī, as well as the nectar, the supreme essence. 96.
Everything—including gods, asuras, and humans—has arisen from the nectar;
and the thirteenth stage is renowned as the auspicious Vajradharī-bhūmi. 97.
Arising in the form of a triangle, she is known as Dharmodayā;
filled with moon, sun, and water, she is the embodiment of Prajñā, most brilliantly radiant. (98)
From bliss—that which is the greatest of all joys—arises that which brings about the attainment of Buddhahood;
there, in the center, is situated the great lotus with ten million petals.
Always accompanied by the vowels and consonants beginning with *ka* and *sa*, it is covered by the cloths of the moon and sun, and endowed with the ninefold wisdom (*prajñā*). || 100 ||
It is the flowing [stream], having the form of fire, the supreme arising of the moon of the bindu;
it generates bliss, is divine, and bestows the fruit of all goals without exception. || 101 ||
The abode of the glorious Sukhavajrin is pure like nectar, full, endowed with precious jewels, and the support of infinite qualities. 102.
She is the cause of all delight, the agent of creation and dissolution,
and she possesses the forms of many deities, born from the ocean and the fire.
The form of the enjoyment of the Dharma and the emanation body itself turn the wheel of Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings in manifold ways. || 104 ||
The world-systems throughout the ten directions, extending to their infinite limits, are everywhere endowed with the ten powers of knowledge; he is the supreme one, preeminent in wisdom. (105)
The element of space is the stable lotus path, arrived through the auspicious succession;
likewise, there are the lotus of the womb, the lotus of the navel, and the lotus of the throat. (106)
Those who are well-established in their perceptions see the sixty-fold [elements], the lotus, and that which is situated at the lateral gate, as well as the resonance. || 107 ||
The attachment to the nine gates through which feces, urine, and semen flow is like a spider's web, extending both downward and upward. (108)
They are renowned as Prajñās, the mothers of all Buddhas;
in their midst stands the deity, the non-dual Supreme Lord.
The Omniscient One sports in great bliss within the three lotuses, which are beautifully adorned by Fire, Water, Indra, and Wind. || 110 ||
Being slowly rotated with skill, it is led through the three lotuses by means of the nostril application via the path of the opening of the uvula. || 111 ||
The non-dual Buddha, being measured within the opening of the *nālikā*-vajra, having been divided by the wheel, comes to rest before the *ghaṇṭikā*. 112.
One should drink the nectar by means of the application of the vajra-tongue;
thereupon the body arises pure and naturally stainless. || 113 ||
This yoga, which destroys old age and death and possesses divine wisdom, was taught to me effortlessly by Bhadrapāda. 114.
The samādhi named Amṛta is the truth, the truth; of this there is no doubt.
By the differentiation of the breath, the letter *ha* is indeed the unstruck sound (*anāhata*). (115)
In the channels that pierce the uvula, thirty-two nāḍīs are recognized;
these are declared to be the thirty-two sacred sites, free from parts and non-dual. (116)
By means of the differentiation of the breath through the nose, the letter *ka* is indeed the unstruck sound (*anāhata*);
having led it through the path of the opening of the uvula, one reaches the certain path.
Having rested there at the gateway, [he perceives] the pure form, the luminous, named the beginningless and non-dual, abiding in the form of glorious bliss. || 118 ||
Then, having brought [the breath] to the Māhendra [channel], one should impel the wind;
O Supreme Lord, it certainly bursts open the path of Dhruva when it is not struck. 119.
Having attained the thirteenth stage, he is blissful like another body;
established in primordial perfection, he is the turner of the wheel of Dharma. || 120 ||
The tradition of Bhadrapāda has been thus briefly set forth;
whatever was heard and mastered through the cultivation of hearing and reflection [is here presented]. (121)
Through the grace of Bhadrapāda and by means of the practice of hearing [the teachings], this work titled *Kuddāla* has been composed by me with skill. 122.
May I be the servant of Bhadrapāda and the teacher of other yogins, and may I be so for all sentient beings without exception, birth after birth. (123)
[Ed. p.
208] By means of this resolve: "If I am to become a Buddha, or else go to hell, may hell itself be my Sukhāvatī. (124)

Thus has been written by me, following the lineage of the stainless Guru, the Antaryoga, the doctrine of the true nature of all mantras of vast qualities, and the Arisen Stage (*utpannakrama*), which consists of the inconceivable non-dual portion; this tradition of yoga is for the sake of recollection by those of us born in this age who are dull-witted and of limited intellect, [proceeding] from the form of the deity who is the essence of the *nīti*.
